ritter_dam_break — DRIVE swarmflow op

• Data kinds: signal × scalar × scalar → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.ritter_dam_break(x, t: 'float', h0: 'float', g: 'float' = 9.81, particle_mass=None) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import swarmflow; swarmflow.ritter_dam_break(x, t: 'float', h0: 'float', g: 'float' = 9.81, particle_mass=None) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("ritter_dam_break"))

Usage

Ritter's dam-break solution (shallow-water equations, dry bed, dam at x = 0, water at x < 0).

c₀ = √(g h₀). x ≤ −c₀ t: h = h₀, u = 0 / −c₀ t < x < 2c₀ t: h = (2c₀ − x/t)²/(9g), u = (2/3)(x/t + c₀) / x ≥ 2c₀ t: h = 0.

Near the front h ∝ (x_f − x)², so there is almost no water. The amount of water from the front to δ is ∫₀^δ (s/t)²/(9g) ds = δ³/(27 g t²) (derived). Given the amount per particle m (h₀Δx for 1-D SPH), the location of the foremost particle (where the amount from the front is m/2) x_f − (27 g t² m/2)^{1/3} is returned in lead_particle —— the front of a particle method always appears to lag behind Ritter's front, and the lag can be read from this formula (refining the particles shrinks it only as m^{1/3}).

Returns:

dict: h, u (same shape as x), front = 2c₀ t, rarefaction_head = −c₀ t, c0, lead_particle (when m is given).

Empty input (x with 0 elements) raises ValueError.
